events.title: Chromebook CR-48 pilot begins
events.summary: Google began shipping CR-48 Chromebook prototypes to beta testers in December 2010 — the first Chrome OS laptops.
events.about: The CR-48 had no caps-lock key (replaced with Search), booted to the browser in seconds, and stored everything in the cloud. Developers tested web apps on a laptop that assumed always-on connectivity — foreshadowing Chromebooks in schools and enterprises. Chrome OS later added Android and Linux app support, but the CR-48 proved a browser could be the whole OS.

narrative.whyChosen: The CR-48 pilot launched the Chromebook category and Chrome OS as a laptop platform.
narrative.whyImportant: It validated cloud-first computing for mainstream hardware beyond netbooks.
narrative.problemSolved: Traditional laptops carried slow boot times, heavy local software, and complex IT management.

sources.title: Google Blog — Chrome OS pilot program (December 2010)

events.title: Nexus S released
events.summary: Google began selling the Nexus S — Samsung-built Nexus with NFC and curved glass.
events.about: Nexus and Pixel phones were Google's pure-Android reference hardware for developers. Samsung-built nexus with nfc and curved glass. AOSP builds and CTS testing often used Pixel devices as the baseline.

narrative.whyChosen: The Nexus S was a flagship Google Android reference device.
narrative.whyImportant: Pixel/Nexus hardware defines the reference Android experience for developers.
narrative.problemSolved: Android needed first-party reference phones without OEM skin fragmentation.
